profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite facility is in one of the company confirmed operating markets. Wikipedia coverage states that as of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with key locations including Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York City, Northern Virginia, San Francisco/San Jose, Santa Clara, Atlanta, Orlando, and Washington, D.C. In May 2007 the company acquired Chicago properties as part of a wider expansion. CoreSite began operating a Washington, D.C. facility in August 2005, one of its earliest East Coast sites after founding in 2001 as CRG West. CoreSite rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009, went public in September 2010, and was acquired by American Tower in December 2021. This specific market was confirmed as an active CoreSite location, but no market specific acquisition date or building history beyond the general company timeline was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite Secaucus Campus holds 256,000 square feet of technical space in Hudson County, New Jersey, positioned within a ten-market footprint operated by American Tower (CoreSite's parent since December 2021). The campus power capacity is not published; without a megawatt figure, its scale relative to other hyperscale AI infrastructure cannot be directly compared, though the technical floor space suggests a mid-sized regional facility rather than a purpose-built AI training campus.

The facility qualifies to host financial services, healthcare, and regulated security workloads. It holds SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 attestations, ISO 27001 and NIST 800-53 certifications, and compliance with PCI DSS and HIPAA standards, indicating readiness for banking, payment processing, and patient data applications rather than the unregulated compute-at-scale that drives contemporary AI model training.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data centers, of which five publish power specifications totaling 111.3 MW; CoreSite Secaucus ranks sixth in the state by published capacity, placing it below the state's largest disclosed facilities. Without its own published megawatt figure, the campus does not factor into the state's total compute baseline and cannot be assessed as a constraint or asset for the grid's role in AI scaling.
